title: Chapter 97
content:
The men stepping out from behind the parked vehicles drew long, gleaming sashimi knives from their jackets.

Slipping his suppressed pistol back into his waistband to free up his hands, Jakyeong broke into a full sprint toward the roadster. Figures closed in from both flanks, the narrow driving lanes flashing with the sharp, whistling glints of polished steel.

Jakyeong seized the lead attacker’s forearm, tucked the limb under his armpit, and snapped the joint backward with a brutal, single-motion crunch.

Snatching the dropped blade out of mid-air, he drove the tip straight through the man’s boot into his metatarsals, then whipped the steel upward in a fluid, rising arc that severed the carotid artery in one clean stroke.

Crimson geysered into the concrete gloom. The man collapsed, clutching his spurting throat, thrashing across the floorboards like a landed fish.

Twisting the hilt with a practiced flick of his fingers, Jakyeong hurled the blade across the aisle. The knife buried itself to the hilt in the right eye socket of a second assailant, sending him crashing to his knees with a bloodcurdling scream.

Drawing his sidearm with his right hand, Jakyeong swept the perimeter.

Pfft, pfft.

Muzzle flashes strobed through the shadows as suppressed 9mm rounds punched clean through center mass and foreheads, dropping targets in rapid succession.

Faced with such ferocious, lethal efficiency, several men in the back pulled handguns from their holsters.

Jakyeong dropped flat, sliding beneath the chassis of an adjacent SUV. Leveling his sights along the concrete, he emptied rounds into exposed ankles and shins. As the wounded collapsed screaming to the floor, he methodically ventilated their skulls, surging back to his feet—

CRACK.

A high-velocity slug grazed his cheek, burning the skin.

From behind a conversion van, a shooter with a mask covering the lower half of his face lunged forward. Before the man could line up a second shot, a towering shadow materialized from behind, large hands locking around the gunman's chin and skull to twist the cervical spine with a sickening SNAP.

Kang Il-hyun let the limp body drop, flashing a triumphant, wicked grin.

Jakyeong ground his teeth. When the hell did he sneak all the way over there?!

At this rate, he was genuinely going to be forced into floral lace lingerie tonight. The mere prospect sent a violent shudder down his spine.

Distracted by the wager for a split second, a whistling blade cut within a hair's breadth of his throat.

Dodging the edge by millimeters, Jakyeong caught the attacker's wrist, twisted the knife free, and fractured the man’s nose and windpipe with a vicious double-jab before burying a fist into his hair, slamming the man’s skull through the front windshield of a parked sedan with concussive force.

As he tossed the pulverized body aside, heavy footfalls echoed from the roof of the adjacent car.

A hulking operative in a dark suit dropped down, leveling an automatic sidearm. Jakyeong dove, rolling beneath the undercarriage of a nearby sedan just as a volley of hollow-points tore through the concrete where he had been standing.

Fuck. They brought an entire damn battalion.

Right on cue, the theater doors on the upper level opened, and a crowd of civilian moviegoers began filtering down the pedestrian ramps. The echo of civilian chatter and laughing voices drifted into the garage. Seizing the chaos, Jakyeong rolled from beneath the chassis, staying low.

He bolted between the parked cars under a fresh barrage of gunfire. BANG! BANG! Stray rounds shattered side windows, triggering a symphony of piercing car alarms. Hearing the gunfire, the civilians shrieked in terror, scrambling back toward the stairwells, while the hit team fractured their lines to avoid firing blindly into the crowd.

Mall security guards brandishing nightsticks burst through the double doors, taking one look at the heavily armed killers and immediately scrambling for their radios.

Rounding the final pillar toward the roadster, Jakyeong swept the bay. The garage was absolute pandemonium, but Kang Il-hyun was nowhere in sight.

Did that idiot actually take a round?

The man was far too slippery to go down easily, yet an unwanted spike of panic tightened in Jakyeong’s chest.

He lunged toward the driver’s side, throwing the door open—only to freeze.

Sitting comfortably in the passenger seat with his long legs crossed, smiling like a depraved pervert, was Kang Il-hyun.

"Floral lace for Lee Ja-kyeong, confirmed."

Jakyeong gritted his teeth, thumbing the push-to-start.

The twin-turbo engine roared to life with a ferocious snarl. Slamming the shifter into reverse, Jakyeong swung the tail out, floored the throttle, and shot toward the exit ramp like a ballistic missile.

Behind them, multiple black SUVs peeled out in pursuit.

The roadster obliterated the plastic parking boom gate, bursting out into the blinding afternoon light.

Taking an aggressive right on two wheels, Jakyeong blew straight through a red light, weaving through oncoming traffic.

"How did you reach the car first?" Jakyeong demanded.

"I crept through the blind spots."

Jakyeong shot him a look of pure, unadulterated disgust. "Unbelievable. You hid like a coward while I was fighting for my life back there?"

"Combat is about tactical efficiency, darling. Who told you to stand around getting shot at?"

Jakyeong glared sideways. "Just wait. The next time we walk into an ambush, I'm using my 'tactical efficiency' to abandon you first."

"Changing your tune already? Who was the one passionately proposing to protect me this morning?"

Proposing. Engaged. The man’s pathological delusions knew no bounds.

Mouthed curses bled past Jakyeong’s lips as the pursuit thickened in his mirrors. Ahead, downtown gridlock had choked the main boulevard into a standstill.

Without hesitating, Jakyeong yanked the wheel, plunging the roadster into a narrow pedestrian alleyway.

HONK—! HONK—!

The horn blared continuously as pedestrians scattered like the parting of the Red Sea. The pursuit vehicles tore right in behind them. The roadster bucked violently over speed bumps, the suspension bottoming out with bone-rattling impacts each time the tires touched asphalt.

Nearing the mouth of the alley, a delivery van sat idling, completely blocking the lane.

Jakyeong mounted the sidewalk, driving the right flank straight over a raised concrete planter. The roadster launched into the air, cleared the obstruction, and slammed back onto the asphalt with a deafening thud.

Il-hyun instinctively grabbed the overhead handle, a grimace breaking across his sharp features.

"You do possess a valid driver's license, correct?"

"Don't worry," Jakyeong retorted, eyes pinned to the glass. "I might not drive as aggressively as Ryun-ge, but I don't lose tail details."

"Ahead."

"I see it!"

The avenue ahead was equally congested. Jakyeong threaded the needle between two parallel-parked trucks, clearing the gap by a hair's breadth. The impact sheared both side mirrors off in an explosion of plastic, yet the pursuit SUVs remained glued to their bumper.

Reaching a four-way intersection, Jakyeong moved to cut left, but an interceptor SUV surged from the adjacent lane, cutting off the turn and forcing them straight ahead toward an arterial tunnel.

Spotting the tunnel entrance signs, Jakyeong glanced across the console.

Il-hyun looked entirely unbattered—lounging against the leather like a man playing a high-stakes arcade game.

Snatching the spare loaded sidearm from his jacket, Jakyeong shoved it into Il-hyun's palm.

"See the tunnel? Once we're inside, take out their tires."

Il-hyun gave a calm nod.

Plunging into the subterranean gloom, Il-hyun rolled down his window, leaning out to level the muzzle at the lead pursuit vehicle.

Pfft, pfft, pfft.

Sparks showered off the asphalt as suppressed rounds punched into the SUV's front bumper and grille, yet the tires remained entirely untouched.

Jakyeong glanced in the rearview mirror and scowled. "What kind of pathetic marksmanship was that?!"

"The target is moving, darling."

"It's a car! If it wasn't moving, it wouldn't be a chase!"

"Keep nagging me and I'll put the next round through your shoulder."

"You—!"

BANG! BANG!

A hail of return fire struck their rear window. While the reinforced ballistic glass held, the remaining glass housing was pulverized.

Jakyeong snatched the pistol back, grabbing Il-hyun’s wrist and slamming his hand onto the steering wheel.

"Hold the wheel!"

Jakyeong thrust his upper body out of the driver's side window, leveling the sidearm with both hands.

He squeezed the trigger.

The front-left tire of the lead pursuit SUV detonated. The heavy vehicle pitched violently, fish-tailing across the lanes before slamming into the tiled tunnel wall with concussive force.

The trailing vehicles bottlenecked behind the wreckage, buying them a precious gap.

Jakyeong slipped back into his seat, stomping the gas.

Glancing across, Il-hyun was staring at him with a completely dazed, struck-by-lightning expression—the exact same reverence he had worn when Jakyeong vowed to protect him that morning.

"W-What is it now?"

"Do you have any earthly idea how devastatingly sexy you are right now, darling?"

The unhinged compliment caught Jakyeong completely off guard.

Il-hyun let out a heavy, breathless sigh, muttering to himself:

"Fuck me... I'm rock-hard."

Jakyeong sat in stunned, speechless defeat. The man is a rabid dog in heat.

Before Jakyeong could threaten to shoot his dick off, Il-hyun reached across the console, grasping Jakyeong's hand and murmuring if he could just touch it for five seconds.

While Jakyeong was thrashing to swat the groping hand away, SLAM!

A fresh pursuit vehicle rammed their rear bumper from behind.

Jakyeong checked the mirrors—more black sedans had closed the distance. He had never missed Wang Ryun’s wheel-work more in his life.

There were too many of them, and worse, their pursuit pattern was deliberate: at every major fork, interceptors surged forward to block the turns, funneling them strictly down a single, predetermined vector.

"Something's wrong, isn't it?"

"Yeah."

The playful sleaze vanished from Il-hyun's face, replaced by an arctic, razor-sharp chill. The sudden shift in pressure made Jakyeong’s grip on the wheel tighten.

To make matters worse, the bruised sky opened up, unleashing a furious downpour.

The torrential rain blinded the windshield, rendering the wipers useless. Every high-speed drift sent the roadster sliding across standing water.

Yet at some point, the trailing cars stopped firing, simply shadowing their rear at a fixed distance.

A coordinated perimeter...

"They're herding us," Il-hyun said, his baritone cold as a grave.

Jakyeong clamped his jaw shut.

Recognizing the gravity of the containment, Il-hyun dialed Park Tae-soo for emergency tactical extraction, then leaned out into the blinding deluge with the sidearm.

Pfft. Pfft. Pfft.

Three consecutive shots punched cleanly through three tires, sending pursuit vehicles spinning off the asphalt in violent succession. Il-hyun swapped magazines with blinding, mechanical precision—fluid, lethal, and flawless.

Jakyeong stared in mild disbelief. So the earlier missed shots were just him playing around.

Once the final magazine ran dry, their pursuers had been whittled down to a third.

Yet the remaining chase team reorganized their lines without hesitation, maintaining the perimeter. These were elite, disciplined operators; returning home in one piece today was not going to be a simple affair.

Breaking out into the desolate outskirts of the city, the rain continued to hammer the earth beneath a pitch-black sky.

Suddenly, the pursuit vehicles began dropping back, reducing their speed.

Just as Jakyeong focused on the rearview, Il-hyun barked:

"Brake! Now!"

Jakyeong caught sight of the spiked steel strip stretched across the asphalt, but it was already too late.

BANG-BANG!

Both front tires shredded instantly. The roadster lost all stability, hydroplaning across the slick tarmac before slamming violently into the industrial guardrail.

The chassis buckled, but the low speed of the impact kept the cabin intact.

We can still fight on foot, Jakyeong thought, reaching for his spare blade.

The brief hope died in the next heartbeat.

A battery of high-intensity stadium floodlights mounted on flatbed trucks erupted around the perimeter, bathing the wreckage in a blinding, white-hot glare.

Jakyeong shielded his eyes with his forearm.

Beside him, Il-hyun hissed a venomous curse:

"Fuck."

Without waiting, Il-hyun threw his arms around Jakyeong, pulling the boy's head down beneath his chest just as an ear-splitting, sustained volley of automatic gunfire pulverized the roadster.

The reinforced ballistic glass shattered into powder, the leather seats torn to shreds by hundreds of rounds. The concussive roar inside the cabin sounded like iron ball bearings rattling in a steel drum.

The deafening storm of lead abruptly ceased.

Breathing in ragged, shallow gasps, Il-hyun and Jakyeong slowly raised their heads.

The halogen searchlights cut through the rain.

Surrounding the totaled sports car in a flawless, impenetrable circle were dozens of heavily armed paramilitary contractors, assault rifles leveled with lethal discipline.

And standing dead in the center, sheltered beneath a black umbrella held by a retainer, towering like the grim reaper himself, was Chairman Kang.
